record.paper_title: Open questions in QCD at high parton density
record.context_brief: Linear versus nonlinear description of inclusive e+A DIS
record.original_question: If nonlinear running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov evolution successfully predicts nuclear-to-proton structure-function ratios in inclusive electron-nucleus deep inelastic scattering, can the linear EPS09 nuclear parton-distribution approach simultaneously accommodate both F2 and FL electron-nucleus data when saturation sets in according to the rcBK prediction, or would failure to do so make the rcBK-based description uniquely favored? Here F2 and FL are the two structure functions whose linear combination gives the total virtual-photon–nucleus cross section and which provide access to integrated quark and gluon distributions, respectively.

evidence.quote: Inclusive DIS is pictured in Fig. 4 (left). This process consists in measuring the total γ∗+A cross section, a linear combination of two observables: the F2 and FL structure functions. These provide access to the integrated (with respect to the transverse dynamics) distributions of quarks and gluons respectively.

The approach based on non-linear small-x evolution (rcBK [12]) is predictive, and therefore would undergo a stringent test. If successful, then a further question can be asked: can the linear EPS09 approach [13] (whose errors will be reduced by p+A constraints once LHC data are available) simultaneously accommodate F2 and FL e+A data, if saturation sets in according to the rcBK prediction? If not, then the latter would provide the unique data description.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider inclusive deep inelastic scattering of electrons off a nucleus A, e+A → e+X. The total virtual-photon–nucleus cross section is a linear combination of two structure functions, F2^A(x,Q^2) and FL^A(x,Q^2), which encode (after integration over transverse dynamics) information about quark and gluon distributions in the nucleus, respectively.

Two theoretical descriptions of these structure functions are considered:

(i) A nonlinear small-x description based on the running-coupling Balitsky–Kovchegov (rcBK) evolution equation for the dipole–nucleus scattering amplitude N(x,r), with appropriate initial conditions parametrizing the nuclear saturation scale Q_s,A(x). This approach predicts the onset of gluon saturation at sufficiently small x and yields concrete predictions for nuclear-to-proton ratios of structure functions.

(ii) A linear description based on collinear factorization with nuclear parton distribution functions of EPS09 type, in which F2^A and FL^A are computed via DGLAP evolution from a global fit of nuclear PDFs (whose uncertainties may be further constrained by future proton–nucleus data).

Suppose that, in a kinematic regime where the rcBK description predicts the onset of saturation, the rcBK approach successfully reproduces measured nuclear-to-proton structure-function ratios in inclusive e+A DIS. The question is:

Can the linear EPS09-type nuclear-PDF framework, within its quoted uncertainties, simultaneously fit both F2^A and FL^A data in this same kinematic regime? Equivalently, does there exist a choice of nuclear PDFs consistent with the EPS09 framework that reproduces both F2^A and FL^A measurements when saturation is present according to the rcBK prediction, or is the joint (F2^A, FL^A) data set incompatible with any such linear description, thereby singling out the rcBK-based nonlinear description as the unique adequate one?
artifact.status_search_result: The question depends on simultaneous high-precision measurements of F2 and FL in electron-nucleus DIS, which require a future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC); such data do not yet exist as of 2026. EIC science papers and projection studies (e.g., 1708.05654 and the EIC White Paper) continue to discuss EPS09-type linear nPDF predictions versus rcBK saturation predictions as distinguishable scenarios to be tested, indicating the question remains open pending EIC operation.

status_evidence.title: Nuclear Structure Functions at a Future Electron-Ion Collider
status_evidence.snippet: Projections compare linear nPDF (EPS09-type) predictions and nonlinear small-x (saturation/rcBK) predictions for F2 and FL in e+A DIS at the EIC.
status_evidence.claim: Distinguishing EPS09-type linear nPDFs from rcBK saturation predictions via F2 and FL is presented as a goal for future EIC measurements, not yet settled.

status_evidence.title: Electron-Ion Collider White Paper (arXiv:2211.02785)
status_evidence.snippet: The EIC will measure inclusive nuclear structure functions F2^A and FL^A to test gluon saturation against linear nPDF descriptions.
status_evidence.claim: Resolution of the linear-vs-nonlinear question for inclusive e+A DIS awaits EIC data, indicating the problem is still open.
